key_insight: UI-Zoomer uses model uncertainty at test time to decide whether and where to crop and re-run inference, adaptively zooming only when the model is unsure to improve localization of small icons and dense GUI layouts — without any extra training.
problem_solved: Existing test-time zoom-in methods apply fixed, uniform crops for all inputs, wasting compute and often missing tiny or densely packed interface elements. UI-Zoomer targets zooming to only the uncertain cases, improving accuracy on small/dense elements while avoiding unnecessary inference.
method: Estimate per-instance uncertainty from the base GUI grounding model at test time (e.g., low-confidence / high-entropy predictions).
If uncertainty exceeds a threshold, compute an adaptive crop region and re-run inference at higher resolution; otherwise keep the original prediction.
Merge or replace predictions from the zoomed crop back into the full-screen coordinates to produce final localized UI elements.
impact: Delivers better localization for small icons and cluttered interfaces with less average compute overhead, and can be dropped into existing GUI grounding pipelines because it requires no retraining.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: screenshot → model inference → uncertainty check → conditional crop & zoom → fused output.
Before/after example: full-screen detection vs adaptive zoom detection highlighting recovered small icons.
Bar chart: accuracy (or mAP) and average inference cost for baseline uniform zoom, no-zoom, and UI-Zoomer.
Uncertainty heatmap overlay on a GUI screenshot showing where the system triggers zooms.
paper_title: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
paper_authors: Fei Tang, Bofan Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Tongbo Chen, Songqin Nong
